'''Patricia Burchat''' (born 1958) is the Gabilan Professor of Physics at Stanford University who researches [[Particle physics|experimental particle physics]] and [[cosmology]]. She is interested in mapping [[dark matter]] in the universe, and understanding the nature of [[dark energy]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://gender.stanford.edu/people/patricia-r-burchat|title=Patricia R. Burchat - The Clayman Institute for Gender Research|website=gender.stanford.edu|access-date=2016-05-26}}</ref>  She was named a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2001, and a [[Guggenheim Fellow]] in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?burchatp|title=Patricia Burchat - Array of Contemporary American Physicists|website=www.aip.org|access-date=2016-06-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160812065129/https://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?burchatp|archive-date=2016-08-12|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/patricia-burchat/|title=John Simon Guggenheim Foundation. - Patricia Burchat|website=www.gf.org|access-date=2016-05-26}}</ref> In 2012 she became a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://physics.stanford.edu/news/professor-patricia-burchat-named-fellow-american-association-advancement-science|title=Professor Patricia Burchat named Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science. {{!}} Department of Physics|website=physics.stanford.edu|date=November 30, 2012 |access-date=2016-06-23}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Born in 1958, Burchat grew up in [[Barry's Bay]], Ontario, Canada, and attended [[Madawaska Valley District High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Glynn |first=Kate |date=2012-04-04 |title=Searching for the secrets of the universe |url=https://thevalleygazette.ca/searching-for-the-secrets-of-the-universe/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210920195522/https://thevalleygazette.ca/searching-for-the-secrets-of-the-universe/ |archive-date=September 20, 2021 |access-date=2023-03-16 |website=The Valley Gazette |language=en-US}}</ref> In 1981 she graduated with a B.S. in applied science and engineering from the University of Toronto, and earned a Ph.D. in physics at Stanford University in 1986.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://cap.stanford.edu/profiles/frdActionServlet?choiceId=printerprofile&profileversion=full&profileId=55463|title=Profile, Patricia Burchat|website=Stanford University|access-date=2016-06-23}}</ref>

==Career==
Burchat held a postdoctoral fellowship at the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]] from 1986 to 1988, after which she joined the faculty until 1995.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://inspirehep.net/author/profile/P.R.Burchat.1|title=Burchat, Patricia Rose - Profile - INSPIRE-HEP|website=inspirehep.net|access-date=2016-06-24}}</ref> She has been a member of the Stanford Physics faculty since 1995,<ref name=":2" /> and served as the chair of the department from 2007 to 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://web.stanford.edu/dept/physics/people/faculty/burchat_patricia%20-%20Copy.html|title=People - Patricia Burchat|website=Stanford University - School of Humanities and Sciences|access-date=2016-06-23|archive-date=February 6, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170206105323/https://web.stanford.edu/dept/physics/people/faculty/burchat_patricia|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Research ==
Burchat has been a member of multiple particle physics experiments, including the Mark{{nbsp;}}II experiment at the [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory|SLAC]] [[Linear particle accelerator|Linear Collider]] and the E791 experiment at [[Fermilab]]. She was a founding member of the  [[BaBar experiment]] at SLAC<ref name=":1" /> which explored [[fundamental interaction|fundamental particle interaction]]s, especially the [[weak interaction]]. In these experiments she researched [[W and Z bosons|Z bosons]] as the carriers of the [[weak interaction]], heavy neutral [[lepton]]s, [[semileptonic decay]] of charm [[meson]]s, charm mixing, [[CP violation|CP violations]] in [[B meson]] decays, and differences in the way [[matter]] and [[antimatter]] evolved in time.<ref name=":1" />

Burchat has also been interested in investigating the cosmological evolution of the Universe. She joined the international community developing the [[Large Synoptic Survey Telescope]], aiming to study gravitational bending of light by [[dark matter]] and the evolution of [[dark energy]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Patricia Burchat - Department of Physics |url=https://physics.stanford.edu/people/faculty/patricia-burchat |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170911111200/https://physics.stanford.edu/people/faculty/patricia-burchat |archive-date=2017-09-11 |access-date=2016-06-24 |website=physics.stanford.edu}}</ref> Her 2008 TED talk, "Shedding light on dark matter", explores these two components making up about 96 percent of the universe.<ref>{{Citation|last=Burchat|first=Patricia|title=Shedding light on dark matter|date=February 2008|url=https://www.ted.com/talks/patricia_burchat_shedding_light_on_dark_matter?language=en|access-date=2016-06-24}}.</ref>

== Awards and honors ==

* 2020 — Engineering Alumni Hall of Distinction Award, University of Toronto 
* 2012 — Fellow, [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]
* 2010 — Judith Pool Award, Northern California Chapter of the [[Association for Women in Science]] 
* 2007 — Walter J. Gores Award, Stanford University 
* 2006 — Gabilan Professor of Physics, Stanford University 
* 2005 — [[Guggenheim Fellowship|Guggenheim Fellow]], Stanford University (2005)
* 2004 — Sapp Family University Fellow in UG Education, Stanford University 
* 2001 — Fellow, [[American Physical Society]], cited "For her contributions to the understanding of heavy quark physics, particularly in semileptonic weak decays, in mixing of neutral D and B mesons, and in CP violation."
